## Design

### 2026-10-25 – So I started brainstorming ideas for the project and landed on a simple recorder idea, it records sounds and records it to an SD card, so as usual I brainstormed, landed on a basic idea:

**4h**

So I started brainstorming ideas for the project and landed on a simple recorder idea, it records sounds and records it to an SD card, so as usual I brainstormed, landed on a basic idea:

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 143749](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/7de34253be43af84f59183217ad7199ce5b261354115063b78028f1be4e598a6.png)

Then I found out wait, the ESP32 doesn't have a built in usb so I need one, so I attached, one and it would simply allow me to program the ESP32, and power it.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 143915](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/bef8c4ad55d420342deb974d01aebf12f853ad1360da89319e70d901dcd8c8f1.png)

Then I found out you can use put any USB you need to use a converter; it can't just power the ESP32, it had to also send it data.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 144227](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/9091de166c0f37ded3cd848d28b4455f2a9ff2dae90c3d0e5d700c0bc46dd4a3.png)

Then I did some research about the ESP32s and I found a really simple one, it's called ESP32-S3-Zero, its a really small board, and it very capable for my project, doesn't so much stuff, its super cool and thank god I found out about this, It would be so annoying to wire even more stuff.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/77f66dce66c8677cd181d91ca4a915947e36e6a4b00872c25bc0a61c5972cac6.png)

### 2026-10-25 – Started the Ki cad process, kind of therapeutic, but annoying if it doesn't work. So, I did so research for the right ESP32 and again landed on the S3-Zero, my board is sort of a breakout board, so it

**7h**

Started the Ki cad process, kind of therapeutic, but annoying if it doesn't work. So, I did so research for the right ESP32 and again landed on the S3-Zero, my board is sort of a breakout board, so it's really simple to build it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/020b285e262499f64adedab066ac2ba81789b95baa8ef2687e867e7e437ef665.png)

Then moved on to researching if I needed capacitors, resistors, I also added a push button that would record when I push and when I release it won't record.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 152745](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/dd75aa2dd00840009fb12eabdea3b2217e86976c63152950ffaada6374b495bd.png)

Then I wired the components without the resistor, its just easier for me to wire it, like i wire everything, then just slide in a resistor or a capacitor and its chilling, just helps me keep track of everything.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 153849](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/7dc12f71646b611e1704f19cafa42985fd5256bc31a0d6b2a29a7e23c6ed53d2.png)

Then I remembered the basis of my idea: IM RECORDING IT! but I didn't have an SD card, and so I put an SD card and just searched up the pin outs, honestly, I had no clue on how to do the pin outs for an SD card but yet.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 164838](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/019d200687e2609ed7f70a97899e64cca7cb234bec4610be4a451c909d02e0b9.png)

Then I added the power things for the ERC checker to not like tweak out but it still did, it was two, not a 36 like my last PCB (Phew) If I have 36 I would just move on ATP, I knew I would be screwed, but no the PCB gods were on my side thankfully.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 195348](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/e651f6f7626fa70953129b155b7f99be517f087a32d3fa0643eb3e5e8b11f011.png)

The errors were power errors again they happen a lot of cause Idk how to fix em, but it isn't that much of a problem.

this was the final before I move onto the footprints which are a whole another story.

### 2026-10-25 – Had to do some quick final touches for this schematic, since when i transferred it to the PCB, some didnt work so it was a footprint problem as usual:

**7h**

Had to do some quick final touches for this schematic, since when i transferred it to the PCB, some didnt work so it was a footprint problem as usual:
![Screenshot 2026-10-25 202307](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/47880c70581d00332cc672a7f4725f589155c4ffc9c378431fae2fb494ef09cc.png)

Then I got all the parts into the PCB editor, and they were all there (phew):

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 203859](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/f0c2f9e88bcae1d187c589ddff095fb6926667ba60d1293af6ffbd0d418da53a.png)

There were a lot of overlapping stuff, so I just did as much as I could with front copper traces, and it was a lot, like, a lot. I watched a video wear your supposed to keep the length of the traces the same, yeah about that, I range from 2 mm to 200mm, I said it's fine.......hopefully. ANYWAY!

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 212153](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/1e7647516b5a32c405eca4c21dbc79ee3de43cf5d54c0331caece5e64f421817.png)

Then I moved to the back copper traces. There wasn't that much of these, so it was pretty easy to do.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 212208](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/30d118668322e48c3119e18f6a6115244067582dca9a166a11a9acfb6cd1d82f.png)

These are the final traces:

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 212208](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/30d118668322e48c3119e18f6a6115244067582dca9a166a11a9acfb6cd1d82f.png)
